adaptive_behaviour.note: Weights that differ between images show the selector is input-dependent; they do NOT show the mixture helps. Only the paired comparison answers that. A selector collapsed onto one circuit is a fixed circuit with extra parameters; one that stayed uniform is an unweighted average.

cost.note: All circuits execute on every forward pass. The adaptive condition does NOT skip circuits and performs no conditional execution, so it costs roughly five simulator evaluations per image against one for each fixed condition.

notes.terminology: All circuits execute on every image. The adaptive condition applies a learned per-image softmax over their outputs. This is an adaptive soft mixture of quantum circuits - not dynamic circuit selection, not conditional quantum execution, and not attention.
notes.scope: The Step 11 spatial gate is inside the Step 12 branch and is held identical across all four conditions (56,227 parameters, the large majority of the model). This experiment therefore measures circuit-mixture adaptivity ONLY. It does not show that the model as a whole is more powerful because of adaptivity, and must not be reported as though it did.
notes.capacity: The conditions are NOT parameter-matched. The adaptive condition carries 104 quantum parameters against 8-24 for the fixed ones, and is the larger model overall by at most 356 parameters (0.49%). The gap runs in the adaptive condition's favour and is reported rather than assumed away.
notes.quantum_share: Quantum parameters are a very small fraction of the model. A null result here is unsurprising and remains a valid, reportable outcome.
notes.split: Everything is computed on the val split. This is an architecture question, like Steps 6, 8, 13 and 14, so the internal test set stays sealed for Step 16 and no test metric was read.
notes.family: Three primary comparisons - the mixture against each fixed circuit - form one Holm-corrected family. The fixed-versus-fixed comparisons are descriptive and carry no p-value; promoting them would double the family.
